base64/valid.description: True iff base64/decode would succeed on the string (standard base64 decoding to valid UTF-8); null is false

behavior/apply.description: Record overrides on a behavior value and return the new value of the same kind. A trait value takes the §8 trait-reference surface (config, events and fields merge key-wise, the later value winning; listens, emitsScope and linkedEntity replace); an orbital value takes the §8b import body (maps merge key-wise, traits per trait, extend and retype by field name, the rest replaces). Nothing is resolved until the value is bound or evaluated.

params.name: value
params.description: A trait value or an orbital value

params.name: overrides
params.description: The LOLO §8 trait-reference overrides (trait value) or the §8b import body (orbital value)

behavior/catalog.description: List the installed behaviors under registry folders (`<prefix>/<topic>[/<tier>]`), optionally narrowed by exposure. Each entry carries its traits as values and its shipped embedding vectors.

params.name: scope
params.description: Registry folders and an optional exposure filter

behavior/compose.description: Compose N orbitals into one application schema. Wires events, picks layout, generates pages.
behavior/compose.title: Compose

params.name: config
params.description: ComposeBehaviorsInput: { appName, orbitals[], layoutStrategy?, eventWiring?, entityMappings? }

behavior/dependencies.description: A program's dependency graph: each orbital's `uses` imports, then every installed behavior they reach, with its layer (io, std, a std UI primitive, or unknown) and its own imports.

params.name: program
params.description: A quoted program (as written, with its `uses`)

behavior/describe.description: Describe a trait value (its knobs, the events it emits and listens to, its transition events, and the shipped knob embedding vectors), or an orbital value or a whole behavior `{ behavior }` (its app knobs and, per orbital, its knobs, primary entity fields, the entities it borrows from sibling orbitals, its traits and pages).

params.name: value
params.description: A trait value, an orbital value, or { behavior }

behavior/detect-layout.description: Auto-detect layout from orbital count and wiring topology. Returns single, tabs, sidebar, dashboard, or wizard-flow.
behavior/detect-layout.title: Detect Layout

behavior/pipe.description: Left-to-right composition. Each step receives the previous result as its first arg.
behavior/pipe.title: Pipe

params.name: seed
params.description: Initial value to pipe through steps

params.name: ...steps
params.description: Functions, each receiving the previous result as first argument

behavior/ref.description: A whole behavior as a value (`.lolo` type `behavior`), named by its specifier: `<prefix>/<name>`, `std/behaviors/<name>`, or a workspace-relative `./<dir>/<name>` (what `program/eval` wrote). A literal specifier is resolved when the program is checked; a computed one when the value is mounted. Embedding the value in a render tree runs the whole program in place, with its own pages.

behavior/resolve.description: The behavior a trait value, an orbital value or `{ behavior }` names, resolved: every import and composed trait inlined, as a quoted program.

params.name: value
params.description: A trait value, an orbital value, or { behavior }

behavior/source.description: The behavior a trait value, an orbital value or `{ behavior }` names, as a quoted program.

params.name: value
params.description: A trait value, an orbital value, or { behavior }

behavior/wire.description: Apply cross-orbital event wiring. Adds external emits/listens to inline traits.
behavior/wire.title: Wire

params.name: wiring
params.description: Array of EventWiringEntry { from, event, to, triggers }

browser/beacon.description: POST text to an absolute http(s) URL as text/plain without waiting for a reply: the browser beacon queue first, then one keepalive cors fetch (status only; the body is never read). The URL origin must be declared in egress and a relative URL is refused. Resolves with { sent, via, status, key } via the trailing { emit } envelope; a queue acceptance is { sent: true, via: queue, status: null }. Cancelling stops waiting but never aborts the queue or the fetch. A host without a beacon port emits failure kind unavailable.

params.name: url
params.description: Absolute http(s) URL: a string literal or a url-typed @config knob

params.name: request
params.description: The request: { text } is the body (required); { key } optionally names the call and is echoed in the result

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/clipboard-read.description: Read text from the system clipboard (navigator.clipboard.readText / host clipboard). Requires a user gesture and clipboard permission. Resolves with the clipboard text via the trailing { emit } envelope.
browser/clipboard-read.title: Clipboard Read

browser/clipboard-write.description: Write text to the system clipboard (navigator.clipboard.writeText / host clipboard). Requires a user gesture. Emits success/failure via the trailing { emit } envelope.
browser/clipboard-write.title: Clipboard Write

params.name: text
params.description: Text to write to the clipboard

browser/embed.description: Ask the host's on-device embedder for one vector per text. Resolves with { embeddings, key } via the trailing { emit } envelope, the vectors in input order; an empty list resolves with no vectors without asking the host. Keyed and cancellable like call-service. A host with no embedder wired in emits failure { error, kind: unconfigured, key }; an embedder that errors emits kind failed. The vectors are handed back as the host answered them; the program checks their count. Client only.

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/geolocation-current.description: Read the current device position (navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition / host geolocation). Requires location permission. Resolves with { latitude, longitude, accuracy } via the trailing { emit } envelope.
browser/geolocation-current.title: Geolocation Current

params.name: options
params.description: Optional PositionOptions: { enableHighAccuracy?: boolean, timeout?: number, maximumAge?: number }

browser/open-file-picker.description: Open the OS file picker (window.showOpenFilePicker / host dialog). Resolves with the selected file metadata list, or emits failure when the user cancels or the capability is denied. Async; use the trailing { emit } envelope for success/failure events.
browser/open-file-picker.title: Open File Picker

params.name: options
params.description: Optional picker config: { multiple?: boolean, accept?: string, types?: Array<{description, accept}> }

browser/page-facts.description: Read the requested page facts (hostname, referrer, screenWidth) in list order. Resolves with { available, hostname, referrer, screenWidth } via the trailing { emit } envelope; a fact that was not requested keeps its default and is not readable. Without a page (no window or document) available is false, hostname and referrer are empty and screenWidth is null. A getter that throws emits failure { error }, which is not the no-page outcome.

params.name: fields
params.description: A non-empty, duplicate-free list of bare words from hostname | referrer | screenWidth; the list order is the read order

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } is a non-empty string echoed as key in the success and failure payloads (absent: no key field); { emit: { success, failure } } routes the facts and the { error } failure

browser/prompt.description: Ask the host's on-device model for a reply to the text that satisfies the JSON Schema text. Resolves with { reply, key } via the trailing { emit } envelope: reply is the model's raw JSON text, which the program reads with json/parse under its own shape and checks. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }, and a late reply is dropped. A host with no model wired in emits failure { error, kind: unconfigured, key }, one whose model cannot answer now emits kind unavailable, and a model that errors emits kind failed. Client only.

params.name: text
params.description: The prompt text sent to the model

params.name: schema
params.description: JSON Schema text the reply must satisfy: a JSON object, usually built with json/stringify

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/push-subscribe.description: Subscribe this browser to Web Push notifications: registers the shared push service worker, fetches the VAPID public key from the host (/api/push/vapid-public-key — no key material in the schema), and calls PushManager.subscribe. Requires notification permission (user gesture). Resolves with the flat subscription credentials { endpoint, p256dh, auth } via the trailing { emit } envelope — persist them on an owner-scoped entity row and pass them back to the push.send service as subscription: { endpoint, keys: { p256dh, auth } }. Emits failure when the Push API is unavailable, permission is denied, or the host has no VAPID key configured.
browser/push-subscribe.title: Push Subscribe

browser/tab-act.description: Perform an interaction on one element of a tab: click it, focus it, or type text into it. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { tab } and { elementId }, the { action } and, for type, the { text }

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-apply.description: Apply a visual treatment to one element of a tab (hide, blur, highlight or label it, or restore it). The treatments are a closed set: no arbitrary styles or scripts. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { tab } and { elementId } from tab-query or a watch, the { treatment }, and an optional { label } shown with the element

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-apply-many.description: Apply a list of treatments in one ask per tab. An element that left the page, or a tab that closed, is listed in missing instead of failing the rest. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { items } each { tab, elementId, treatment, label? }

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-capture.description: Capture what a tab shows: the host brings the tab to the front of its window and captures the window, as png (the default) or jpeg (an optional quality from 0 to 100). Hands back { tab, format, image, key } with the image as bytes. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab the browser will not capture kind not-ready. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { tab }, an optional { format } (png or jpeg) and, for jpeg, an optional { quality } from 0 to 100

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-close.description: Close a tab. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { tab } is a tab number from tab-open or tab-list

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-list.description: List the open browser tabs, optionally only those whose URL matches a Chrome match pattern. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { match? } is a URL match pattern such as https://example.com/*

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-navigate.description: Point an existing tab at an absolute URL. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { tab } and the absolute { url } to load

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-open.description: Open a URL in a new tab, adding the params to its query string. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { url } is absolute; { params? } are added to the query string, encoded; { match? } is the pattern the final URL must lie in; { active? } focuses the tab (default false)

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-query.description: Read the elements of a tab's page that match a selector, each with the declared fields, optionally waiting for the page to load and a first match to appear. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { tab }, the CSS { selector }, the { fields } map of name to { selector?, attr?, resolve?, template?, required? }, optional { limit } and { waitMs }

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-unwatch.description: Stop a watch started with tab-watch. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { watchId } is the id tab-watch resolved with

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

browser/tab-watch.description: Watch every tab whose URL matches a pattern for elements matching a selector: each element is reported once, now and as the page changes, to the declared external input the event address names, as { tab, elementId, url, fields }. Asking again for the same watch from the same trait returns the same watchId. Resolves with the shape it produces via the trailing { emit } envelope. Keyed and cancellable like call-service: (cancel-call key) aborts the ask and fires emit.cancelled with { key }. A request outside its closed keys, or a value the kernel refuses, emits failure { error, kind: invalid, key } and asks the host nothing; a host with no browser tabs emits kind unavailable, a tab with no page script kind not-ready, an element that left the page kind not-found. The kernel validates and shapes; the host only performs raw tab and page operations. Client only.

params.name: request
params.description: { match } is the pages to watch, the CSS { selector }, the { fields } to read and the { event } address (Trait.EVENT) of a declared external input

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { key } names the call for cancel-call and is echoed as key; { emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } routes the result

bytes/at.description: The byte at index i as a number 0-255; null when i is outside the data (negative included). A non-whole index fails with kind invalid. A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

bytes/concat.description: Join byte values in order into one bytes value. A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

bytes/equals.description: Whether two bytes values hold the same bytes. A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

bytes/from-string.description: Encode a string as its UTF-8 bytes. A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

bytes/index-of.description: Byte offset of the first occurrence of needle at or after from (default 0; a negative from counts from the end, out-of-range clamps), or -1 when absent. An empty needle answers from. A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

params.name: from
params.description: Byte index to start at; null for 0

bytes/length.description: Number of bytes (not the length of the base64 text). A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

bytes/read-uint.description: The unsigned integer stored in width bytes at offset, big-endian (be) or little-endian (le); null when those bytes run past the data. A width-8 value above 2^53 - 1 fails with kind invalid rather than round. A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte index of the first byte

bytes/slice.description: Bytes from start (inclusive) to end (exclusive, default the length), both counted in bytes. A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

params.name: end
params.description: Byte index to stop before; null for the end

bytes/to-string.description: Decode bytes as UTF-8 text; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 fail with kind invalid. A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

bytes/write-uint.description: A whole number as width unsigned bytes, big-endian (be) or little-endian (le). A value that is negative, not whole, too large for the width, or above 2^53 - 1 fails with kind invalid. A bytes value is a standard padded base64 string at run time.

call-service.description: Invoke an external service action. Optional trailing { key, emit: { success, failure, cancelled } } options object attaches closed-circuit emit routing (V2 frame contract); key names the call for cancel-call.
call-service.title: Call Service

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options object. Set `{ emit: { success: "...", failure: "...", cancelled: "..." } }` to wire closed-circuit result routing (V2 frame), and `key` to name the call for `cancel-call`.

cancel-call.description: Abort the in-flight keyed call started with this key in the same running app: a call-service, an http, a browser/prompt or a browser/embed; a no-op when none is in flight. A list of keys aborts each in turn. The cancelled call emits its declared emit.cancelled event with { key }, never success or failure, and a reply that arrives later is dropped.

params.name: key
params.description: The key the call declared in its options, or a list of keys

credential-forget.description: Drop the signed-in viewer's stored credential named by a secret knob; the success payload is { connected: false, label: "" }. Fails when nobody is signed in.

params.name: credential
params.description: A secret-typed @config knob whose value names the credential

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { emit: { success, failure } } routes the { connected } payload and the { error } failure

credential-list.description: Masked credential inventory: whether the host's credential store can encrypt, the integrations mode, each service's status and every declared credential's source (store, env or none) with its last four characters, never the value. The declared names are the registry's remaining services plus the secret knobs the running program reads. Open to every caller. The success payload is { enabled, mode, services, entries }.

params.name: options
params.description: Optional trailing options: { emit: { success, failure } } routes the result payload and the { error, code } failure

credential-mode.description: Switch the host's integrations mode flag between "mock" and "real"; the host may refuse (mock under production). Requires the caller's @user.role to be one of ALMADAR_CREDENTIAL_ADMIN_ROLES (default admin, owner); fails closed without one. The success payload is { mode }.

params.name: options

postgres.description: Run one read-only SQL statement through the shared kernel: (postgres origin sql params options? options?). The kernel speaks the Postgres wire protocol over the host's raw TCP (an in-band SSLRequest and the kernel TLS when tls is true); the origin must be a postgres:// or postgresql:// origin declared in egress. sql is exactly one SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT): the kernel's read-only guard, the same one orb validate applies to a literal statement, refuses anything else before it connects. params are the bind values $1, $2, ... sent as text for the server to type. options: auth (a secret-typed knob naming the password credential; cleartext, MD5 and SCRAM-SHA-256 logins), user (required), database (default: the user), tls, timeoutMs (the statement timeout), key, emit: { success, failure }. One call is one connection. The success payload is { rows, rowCount, columns, key }: rows are maps of column name to value (booleans, numbers, null, text, lists of those; an int8 past 2^53, numeric, json, jsonb, uuid, date, time, timestamp and every other type as the text Postgres prints; timestamptz as UTC ISO text; bytea as base64), columns are { name, typeOid }. The failure payload is { error, kind, code, credential, key }: kind is refused (egress, grant, the read-only guard or an invalid call), unconfigured, timeout, failed, protocol, unsupported or postgres (the server answered an error; code is its SQLSTATE such as 42P01).

params.description: A postgres:// or postgresql:// origin: a string literal or a url-typed @config knob

params.name: sql
params.description: One read-only SELECT statement, with $1, $2, ... placeholders

params.name: params
params.description: The bind values for the placeholders, in order; null is SQL NULL, a list a Postgres array, an object JSON

params.name: options
params.description: Options: auth (secret knob), user (required), database, tls, timeoutMs, key, emit: { success, failure }

The address is `EVENT`, `Trait.EVENT` or `Orbital.Trait.EVENT` (resolved from the calling trait) and must name a declared external input; the arguments are the payload object or its JSON text (absent or empty is `{}`). An optional `{ schema: [field] }` holds the arguments to a stated payload before dispatch. Success carries `{ result, text }`, the outcome the model is answered with: `{ ok: true, emitted: [{ event, payload? }] }`, or `{ ok: false, error }` for a refusal (an undeclared input, arguments that are not a JSON object, `{ error, issues }` when they miss the schema) or a dispatch that did not take effect (a rejection code, a failed guard, a failed effect, no transition).

The kernel speaks RESP over the host's raw TCP (TLS for rediss://); the origin must be a redis:// or rediss:// origin declared in egress. command is a list of text items (the command name first).
